text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe the specific location of your wrist pain and how it started, such as a recent injury or gradual onset. Also, let me know if you have any numbness or tingling in your fingers.

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's tenosynovitis (likely secondary to previous distal radius fracture), possibly with superimposed trigger thumb or early rheumatoid arthritis given the family history.

I need to confirm if you have pain when moving your thumb against your wrist or if you notice clicking in your thumb joint. Additionally, could you describe the specific sensation of the "fall" six months ago and whether your wrist was swollen then?
